The twenty-four led-arrow, four led-dot and two qsfp-lane-leds placements therefore keep their component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Nine rows elsewhere in those same tables read \"need NOS to activate this feature\", so these may be NOS-defined rather than simply undocumented - which is a different fix, and the reason this is filed as vendor-silent rather than nos-dependent: we do not know which, and guessing would put an answer where the unknown belongs.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["ports","optics"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or from a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with the ports in known states (down, 1G/10G/25G link, traffic)","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"blocks":[],"note":"Searched and absent. The author already drew it as `region:timing` with exactly these five members and had nowhere else to say it","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","model":"S9510-28DC","name":"s9510-28dc","provenance":{"attrs":"datasheet (Specifications/Performance/Accessories sections)","bits-tod-jacks":"estimated (drawing shows compact stacked jacks ~11.5mm tall; modeled as two standard 14mm cutout ports which slightly exceeds the drawn stack - verify against physical unit)","chassis":"datasheet (440 x 302 x 43.5mm, 4.9kg without FRU)","layout":"drawing-inferred (HIG Fig 5/9 front drawing measured at 4.5 px/mm; pending photo overlay calibration - marketing photos are low resolution)","led-semantics":"HIG section 10, pages 20-21, transcribed rather than only cited - the citation was here and the tables were not, so nobody could interpret two of these lamps. Each front-panel lamp carries its own vocabulary: GNSS, SYNC and PWR each draw four distinct meanings out of two colours and two behaviours, which is why a state carries a behavior as well as a color. On PWR, Solid Green is \"system power good\" and Blinking Green is \"power good but BMC power fail\"; a model carrying only colour collapses them into one. The management jack is declared per element because its left lamp is green for 1G and its right amber for 10M/100M. The PSU FRU and Fan FRU tables belong to the modules and are transcribed in their own contracts. The HIG gives NO table for the port lamps, so the twenty-four led-arrow, four led-dot and two qsfp-lane-leds placements keep the component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Corrected after review: qsfp-lane-leds did NOT carry that default when this was written - it still declared off/link/activity, unsourced, and \"link\" had neither a colour nor a base stylesheet rule so it rendered identically to \"off\". Fixed in common/qsfp-lane-leds v1.2.0","part-numbers":"CORRECTED TWICE, and the second correction reverses part of the first, so both are kept. This device listed `PSU-401-DISB-1` / `PSU-401-AISB` and `FAN-402825-HD` here - FRU part numbers in a field whose schema is \"orderable SKUs for this CONFIGURATION: model -> {part, power-cord}\", meaning the CHASSIS. They were a duplicate too: ufispace/psu-401-dc, psu-401-ac and fan-402825 each carry their own in `attrs.model`, which is where a FRU part number belongs. IT WAS NOT HARMLESS. A DCIM exporter reading the first key as the chassis model filed this router as a device type called FAN-402825-HD in both target libraries, and the S9510-28DC appeared in neither under its own name - see roc-ops/ndv#21. A field carrying the wrong KIND of value is worse than an empty one, because every consumer has to guess which kind it got. THE FIRST FIX SAID NO CHASSIS SKU EXISTS AND THAT WAS WRONG. It is a true statement about the HARDWARE INSTALLATION GUIDE - R1.9 names the product `S9510-28DC` in its title, its overview and its dimensions table and prints no orderable number anywhere - and a false one about the world. Two exist and Jason supplied them: `S9510-28DC-BN0B` for DC and `S9510-28DC-BR1B` for AC. Searching one document and concluding the fact does not exist is the same error the gaps register records against the XFP bezel opening, made again here. THE TWO DC CONFIGURATIONS SHARE A SKU because they are one chassis differently populated - `dc-populated` fits optics into the first four SFP28 cages and is not a different thing to order. AC is, and carries its own. That is exactly the distinction #21 collapses on, so the two DC entries should fold into one device type and the AC one should stand alone. SOURCE IS THE OWNER, NOT A DOCUMENT WE HOLD, and that is recorded rather than dressed up: no PDF in `working/intake/ufispace` contains either string. If a UfiSpace ordering guide ever lands, it should confirm these two and may add the regional variants the Edgecore SKUs show for the same class of box. than merely coping.","qsfpdd-port-numbers":"PAID, by fixing the component rather than the labels. Ports 0-3 keep their numbers at baselines 38.1 and 8.8, where the datasheet front figure puts them: the digit is printed on a coloured band just outside each aperture. The band is faceplate paint - vendor-confirmed - so it is now four rects in panel.decor and common/qsfp-cage@2 is 10.18 tall (0.6 flange + the 9.58 std/qsfp-ganged opening) instead of 13.0. Silkscreen paints over decor and under components, so the numbers now read. The cages for ports 0, 1 and 3 did not move. Port-2 is rotate: 180, so its at: is the box top and shortening the box does not free the digit; its at: was recomputed from the new height and lands at 8.8, which puts its aperture 0.08mm lower than the v1 model had it - 0.4 px at the figure's 4.5 px/mm, and the figure is not self-consistent to better than that: it draws the port-2 digit sitting on the aperture edge rather than clear of it. The band is still NARROWER than the aperture (17.1 against 18.5); it is no longer drawn overlapping it","sfp-pitch":"drawing-inferred (~14.45mm ganged - std/sfp cutouts shoulder to shoulder; verify against physical unit)","timing-labels":"drawing - BITS, the up-down pair and TOD are printed in the gutter to the LEFT of the stacked jacks and RIGHT-aligned against them, and the S9510-28DC wordmark ends on the same edge, one line below the lamp stack.
